name: Public Exercise

date.source: The fed's own broadcast graphic, "CWC Public Exercise -- APRIL 19, 1998"; posted to Usenet the same day in two parts.

matches.stipulation: Non-title exhibition, no bearing on records
matches.how: Detson pulled Kingstead's own inverted piledriver (the Showstopper) into a hanging neckbreaker (the Closing Credits) for the pin.
matches.note: The fed's own first-ever match, billed as an exhibition that would not count toward any wrestler's record.

matches.stipulation: Non-title exhibition, no bearing on records
matches.how: Hunter blinded the referee with a British flag, battered Storm with a steel chair, then locked in a modified ankle lock that the referee stopped as a submission.
matches.note: An unusually violent finish for an exhibition: Hunter kept wrenching the hold well after the stoppage, visibly breaking Storm's leg; the broadcast called it possibly career-ending.

matches.stipulation: Non-title exhibition, no bearing on records
matches.how: Doe reversed a powerslam attempt and hit his own airplane-spin powerslam (the Manic Rage) for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Non-title exhibition, no bearing on records; main event
matches.how: Leviathan connected with a spinning heel kick (the Whirlpool Kick) for the pin after both men traded near-falls.

appearances.source: the broadcast's own credits, served at /promotions/cwc-championship-1998/archive/cwc-championship-public-exercise-1998-04-19.html

notes: The fed's own first public exhibition, staged at Wrigley Field in Chicago and billed as having no bearing on any wrestler's record; four matches introducing eight of the fed's own early wrestlers. Lord Pierce Hunter's chair-assisted leg injury to Tommy Storm was shockingly violent for a supposedly harmless exhibition.

name: Sunday Night Madhouse

date.source: The fed's own broadcast graphic, "Market Square Arena -- May 3"; posted to Usenet in three parts on 4 May 1998, billed on-air as the fed's own first-ever edition of Sunday Night Madhouse.

matches.how: Dumars hit a Tiger Driver (the Dumars Drop) for the fed's own first-ever match win, despite Walker resorting to brass knuckles mid-match.
matches.note: Havoc ran in after the bell and attacked both men with a steel chair, opening a feud with Dumars.

matches.how: Turner won by ten-count knockout after driving Hand through a hot-dog stand in the parking lot.
matches.note: The brawl left the ring, the sound booth, and the parking lot in its wake before ending outside the arena entirely.

matches.how: Kingstead forced a submission with a modified Boston crab (the Ring O' Fire).
Donaven pinned Gonzalez with a DDT (the Donaven Drop) after absorbing a string of no-sold power moves.
Jim finished the Masked Judge with his superkick, the Final Judgement.
matches.note: After the bell, Jim handcuffed the Masked Judge to the ropes; CWC president Jean Watts stopped the beating, then Pedigreed valet Monique when she confronted her.

matches.how: Woobs appeared to score the pin with a Northern Lights suplex, but the referee ruled both men's shoulders were down for the count and awarded the fall to Nitaya on a technicality.
matches.note: Neptune Nitaya was attacked backstage before the show by a man in a Leviathan mask and costume, who battered his knee with a lead pipe; the CWC's own broadcast did not confirm the attacker's identity.

appearances.source: the broadcast's own credits, served at /promotions/cwc-championship-1998/archive/cwc-championship-sunday-night-madhouse-1998-05-03.html
the broadcast's own credits, served at /promotions/cwc-championship-1998/archive/cwc-championship-sunday-night-madhouse-1998-05-03.html

notes: The fed's own first house show billed as counting toward the record, at Market Square Arena. Leviathan's own appearance here is an angle only: a man in his mask and costume attacked Neptune Nitaya backstage before the show, but the broadcast stopped short of confirming Leviathan himself was responsible.

name: Sunday Night Madhouse

date.source: Posting date of the fed's own three-part broadcast (10 May 1998), billed on-air as the CWC World Title Tournament's first-round matches.

matches.how: Havoc reversed a series of near-falls and got the three count after Grimshaw's own sunset flip was turned back over twice.
Bowers hit Rex with a chair from the apron, toppling him onto his own partners for a fluke three count.
matches.note: Dragonfire's Linebacker wrestled hurt on a bad knee for most of the match after Bowers targeted it early.

matches.how: Smith knocked Hand out with his own Bible, then finished him with a superplex (the Saving Grace).

matches.stipulation: CWC World Title Tournament, first round
matches.how: Doe was disqualified after hitting the referee with the ring stairs; Prime Time was awarded the match.
matches.note: Immediately afterward, rookie Ares challenged both men to an impromptu handicap match for the vacated tournament spot.

matches.stipulation: Handicap match for the tournament spot vacated by the prior match's disqualification finish
matches.how: Ares pinned both Prime Time and "Maniac" John Doe in succession with the same swinging full-nelson slam.
matches.note: Ares' debut win claimed the tournament spot outright, replacing both Prime Time and John Doe in the bracket.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Title Tournament, first round
matches.how: Nitaya finished Hunter with a roundhouse kick to the throat (the Windjammer) despite wrestling on a knee injured backstage before the show.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Title Tournament, first round
matches.how: Nekrataal ambushed Leviathan with a fire extinguisher before the bell and hit a jackknife powerbomb onto it (the Painful Memories); the referee ruled the match a disqualification win for Leviathan.
matches.note: Nekrataal announced afterward that he was abandoning the tournament to pursue a feud with "The Savior" Jebodiah Smith instead.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Title Tournament, first round; main event
matches.how: Jim suplexed the unconscious Garces for the pin (a fisherman's suplex) after valet Monique pulled his foot onto the ropes to save him from an enziguiri pin attempt.
matches.note: Leviathan came to ringside to confront Monique over the interference but was turned away by Jean Watts.

notes: The CWC World Title Tournament's own first round (brackets A-D): Ares, Neptune Nitaya, Leviathan and Crimestarter Jim claimed the four bracket spots. A third edition of Sunday Night Madhouse, which the fed's own fourth-edition recap describes covering the tournament's remaining first-round matches (brackets E-H, won by Paul Kingstead, Steve Dumars, "Blockbuster" Johnny Detson and Havoc), does not survive in the held record.
note: The card itself is not held; the show stands here as a record only.

name: Sunday Night Madhouse

date.source: Posting date of the fed's own three-part broadcast (26 May 1998), billed on-air at the Independence Arena in Charlotte, North Carolina as the fed's own fourth edition of Sunday Night Madhouse and the CWC World Title Tournament's own quarterfinals.

matches.how: Keeblor finished Carlucci with a jackknife powerbomb (the Keeblor Bomb).
Duncan won in two minutes and thirty seconds with an inverted bulldog (the End of the Line), billed as the fed's own shortest match to date.
Nekrataal finished Hand with a jackknife powerbomb (the Painful Memories).
matches.note: Jebodiah Smith's followers rushed the ring afterward; the arena lights went out, and when they came back on the ring was empty, with no resolution shown.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Title Tournament, quarterfinal; Falls Count Anywhere
matches.how: Both men were run down by a limousine and beaten with a baseball bat by a man in a Leviathan mask and costume outside the arena; Havoc landed on top of the incapacitated Dumars for a slow three count once the referee revived.
matches.note: Whether the attacker was really Leviathan was never confirmed on the broadcast. Superstars, Incorporated recruited Havoc on-air immediately afterward.

matches.how: Detson rolled through a Kingstead sunset flip attempt for the pin.
matches.note: Manager Mister Dynamic clotheslined Kingstead twice on the outside during the match. Afterward, Kingstead attacked Detson and Dynamic with a steel chair.

matches.how: Jim finished Nitaya with his superkick (the Final Judgement) after valet Monique's loaded-briefcase shot to a downed referee let him avoid a disqualification.
matches.note: Paul Kingstead, still on the warpath from the earlier Detson match, ran in with a chair and hit Jim before the finish, temporarily saving Nitaya; Jean Watts and Monique also brawled at ringside during the match.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Title Tournament, quarterfinal; main event
matches.how: Leviathan spun out of a full nelson attempt into a spinning heel kick (the Whirlpool Kick) for the pin.
matches.note: Nekrataal and the Hardcore Icons attacked Leviathan immediately after the bell.

appearances.source: the broadcast's own credits, served at /promotions/cwc-championship-1998/archive/cwc-championship-sunday-night-madhouse-1998-05-26.html
the broadcast's own credits, served at /promotions/cwc-championship-1998/archive/cwc-championship-sunday-night-madhouse-1998-05-26.html

notes: The CWC World Title Tournament's own quarterfinals, at the Independence Arena in Charlotte, North Carolina, billed as the fed's own fourth edition of Sunday Night Madhouse. Jean Watts announced a six-bracket International People's Championship tournament to be held entirely at the fed's own first pay-per-view, First Night, and a cross-promotional card with the World Wrestling Organization, War of the Ages, for 16 June 1998, plus her own in-ring match against Monique the following week -- none of which is covered by a document in the held record. Superstars, Incorporated (Johnny Detson and Crimestarter Jim, managed by Mister Dynamic) recruited Havoc on-air after his win; his own membership is not confirmed by any document here. The semifinal lineup leaving this broadcast is Havoc, Johnny Detson, Crimestarter Jim and Leviathan.

name: Sunday Night Madhouse

date.source: The fed's own broadcast graphic reads "June 28, 1998... Sunday Night Madhouse"; posted to Usenet in five parts on 1 July 1998.

matches.how: Santoro hit a Diamond Cutter ("the Jackpot"); Hand held his head and walked to the back rather than continue, and was counted out.
Claiborne pinned Gonzalez with a turnbuckle DDT after a long trading of power moves.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Tag Team Title Tournament, first round
matches.how: Ericsson made William Bowers submit to a Cross-Face Clawhold, moments after Sakai's top-rope Sonic Blast had put Bowers down.
matches.note: Modern Day Society's debut, over a Pittsburgh crowd that turned in their favor after the Upstarts insulted the city on arrival.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Tag Team Title Tournament, first round
matches.how: Havoc hit the 450 splash ("the Killah Splash") on Bill Weber for the pin, after Weber had nearly finished Havoc with a shoulderbreaker-tombstone-Oklahoma Slam sequence and Kim's chair shot to Steve Walker turned the match.
matches.note: Superstars, Incorporated -- billed here as Havoc and Crimestarter Jim, managed by Monique and Kim -- advance; Miss Jackilyn brawled with Monique and Kim at ringside throughout.

matches.how: Leviathan pinned Mister Dynamic with the Whirlpool Kick after the champion and Nekrataal briefly teamed up against Dynamic before turning on each other.
matches.note: Johnny Detson had the match scheduled in his own place, refusing to defend the World Heavyweight Championship until the fed's own Prime Time in North America pay-per-view; Nekrataal attacked Detson with a crowbar before the bell after smashing the windshield of a car in the parking lot bearing Havoc's own license plate.

matches.stipulation: Boiler Room Rumble (unsanctioned; the team that leaves the boiler room, and the arena, under its own power wins)
matches.how: Eclipse walked out of the arena lobby on his own power, the last man standing, after the brawl wrecked a boiler room, a service elevator, a lobby full of concession stands and a locker room, sauna and shower.
matches.note: President Jean Watts's own manager, "Warrior" Austin Rage, was knocked out with a chair by Eclipse before the brawl even reached the boiler room; Dragonfire (Rex and the Linebacker) briefly interfered against the Hardcore Icons late in the match, and Jose Garces attacked Eclipse afterward in revenge for an earlier Wrecking Crew assault at the fed's own War of the Ages appearance.

notes: President Jean Watts announced three Summerstorm matches ("The Hardline" Chris Pain vs. Bryan Sweet; Paul Kingstead vs. "Blockbuster" Johnny Detson, best two-out-of-three falls; Mike Sebastian vs. International People's Champion Jose Garces) and confirmed Leviathan's own World Heavyweight Championship defense against Nekrataal at Summerstorm, billed as the "No Way Out" match. Earlier in the broadcast, Jude St. Claire hijacked a scheduled number-one-contender match between Marshall Duncan and Ares to instead air Superstars, Incorporated's own backstage ambush of both men -- Black Diamond chokeslammed Ares, Mister Dynamic worked over Duncan, and Johnny Detson declared himself the new number-one contender over both men's motionless bodies; Paul Kingstead ran in to fight Detson and Crimestarter Jim but was beaten down. Dragonfire (Rex and the Linebacker) confronted Paul Kingstead in a separate segment before attacking him, then later turned on the Hardcore Icons during the Boiler Room Rumble.

name: Prime Time in North America

date.source: The fed's own broadcast graphic and posting date, 21 July 1998; billed as the fed's own first special event held at the Palace of Auburn Hills, Auburn Hills, Michigan, and posted to Usenet in four parts (a duplicated introductory crosspost repeats the opening of part one).

matches.stipulation: Inaugural CWC North American Heavyweight Championship four-way elimination match (two men in the ring at a time, entering by tag)

eliminations.how: counted out after Nekrataal secretly tagged him in while he was still brawling outside with the disguised Strangler
pinned by Lord Keeblor with a Hurricanrana rolled into a cradle

matches.how: Kingstead pinned Lord Keeblor with a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker rolled into a tight package, after the two had briefly teamed to double-suplex Nekrataal.
matches.note: The masked Strangler had ambushed the real Frank Claiborne backstage and wrestled the match's opening minutes disguised as him; a furious Nekrataal powerbombed both Kingstead and Keeblor after his own elimination, in an unpunished post-match assault. Paul Kingstead became the CWC's first North American Heavyweight Champion.

matches.how: St. Claire won by disqualification when a masked security guard, later unmasked as Mike Sebastian, DDT'd and top-rope-splashed him after Garces had been weakened by a guardrail powerbomb from Romulus; the title cannot change hands on a disqualification, so Garces retained.
matches.note: A mystery attacker wearing a masked "Sacrificer" Nekrataal t-shirt handcuffed Romulus to the guardrail mid-match; his identity was never confirmed.

matches.stipulation: CWC World Tag Team Championship (vacant); changed to no-disqualification by President Jean Watts after an initial double count-out
matches.how: Eclipse pinned Earl "The Hammer" Mandigault with a small package after the Frat interrupted a Superstars, Incorporated run-in that had briefly stolen the belts; Latin Lightning and the Baby Face Brawler drove off Havoc and Crimestarter Jim and recovered the belts from Monique and Kim.
matches.note: One of the fed's own most violent matches, spilling through a boiler-adjacent lobby, a locker room, a sauna and a shower before returning to the ring; CWC Talent Coordinator Brandon Newton was knocked out twice trying to keep order. The L.A. Wrecking Crew became the CWC's first World Tag Team Champions; the Frat attacked both battered Hardcore Icons with steel chairs once the match ended.

matches.how: Leviathan hit the real Detson with the Whirlpool Kick for the pin, retaining the title.
matches.note: Superstars, Incorporated had tied up the real Leviathan backstage and sent out Jude St. Claire disguised as him; the disguised St. Claire "lost" the title to Detson in a sham finish before the real Leviathan burst out, unmasked St. Claire with a Whirlpool Kick of his own, and restarted the match for real. Paul Kingstead ran in to fend off Mister Dynamic and St. Claire with his new North American title belt.

notes: The fed's own first special event, crowning champions for two brand-new titles (North American Heavyweight, World Tag Team) and settling neither of its other two title pictures cleanly (the International People's Championship kept its champion on a disqualification; the World Heavyweight Championship was defended only after a stable's own impersonation scheme was exposed). This is the last card in the held record; no further self-issued CWC document survives.
